freeEnergyMeaning: Ideal bulk Gibbs difference G_s-G_n at fixed external field; superconducting branch is not supplied above Tc.
geometryAssumption: Negligible demagnetization, e.g. a long cylinder in longitudinal field; no finite-sample intermediate state.
boundaryMeaning: At nonzero-field coexistence, a unique homogeneous order index is not assigned. No intermediate-state geometry is solved.
speech: Ideal bulk type-I teaching model: negligible demagnetization, fixed Tc = 7.2 K and μ₀Hc(0) = 80 mT. This is not a microscopic prediction for a real specimen. Scroll the plot horizontally to inspect the full 0–10 K range. “Inspect transition” centers the boundary when it exists. At 7.20000 K and μ₀Ha = 0 mT: normal state. Superconducting Gibbs branch unavailable at or above Tc. The gold branch ends at its superconducting one-sided limit. The blue branch is the normal state. Open endpoints at nonzero field indicate coexistence; no sloped line joins the jump and no unique homogeneous order is assigned at that point. The order index √(1−T/Tc) is phenomenological, not a measured energy gap. Finite-sample intermediate domains, surface barriers, hysteresis and type-II vortices are not solved. Transparent wireframe of a displayed segment of an ideal infinite cylinder. Rings mark the viewing window, not physical ends. Blue arrows: B at 10 mm/T display scale. Gold arrows: surface K at 10⁻⁵ mm per A/m. White dots: zero-valued samples. Glyphs are not particle paths. Same spatial scale on all axes. Field and current glyphs use the separately declared value scales. The Gibbs-energy comparison uses Δg = (μ₀Ha² − μ₀Hc²)/2, equivalently [(μ₀Ha)²−(μ₀Hc)²]/(2μ₀), below Tc. Negative favors the superconducting branch. The approximation μ₀ ≈ 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m is used. There is no superconducting-branch energy supplied above Tc.
